# Description
This file enables preprocessing of the TeDDi sample natural language text material (Moran et al., 2022). This is used as a sample to compare against the sign codings for proto-cuneiform and paleolithic sign sequences. Dumps of the TeDDi sample can be downloaded from https://drive.switch.ch/index.php/s/MJv7xFkzqlzFn0y. Note that the sample of TeDDi lines was here produced by using the follwing Perl commands in the directory where the lines.csv file is stored:

head -1 line.csv > line_sample.csv
perl -ne 'print if (rand() < .01)' line.csv >> line_sample.csv

This randomly samples 10% of the overall around 20 million text lines. This downsampling is necessary, since otherwise loading the data into R for further processing is not feasible.

# Preprocessing of Raw Text Lines
The text lines are here further cleaned, since there is some unwanted noise in the character strings. In particular, we use the regex "[[:punct:]]" to remove punctuation from all text lines. While it can be argued that punctuation belongs to writing, the problem is that some text lines consist of only punctuation, e.g. "** *" or a series of symbols for musical notes which are arguably not genuine writing (i.e. not representing speech sounds -- not even in an indirect way). 

We also use the regex "[!-~]" to remove ASCII characters (see table below) from number 33 (exclamation mark) to 126 (tilde) from *non-Latin* scripts. This is because there is -- mainly English -- contamination of texts in other languages and writing systems (e.g. Mandarin Chinese, Korean). Note that this also removes some of the punctuation in the non-Latin scripts.    
```{r foo, out.width="100%", fig.cap="ASCII table from WikiCommons"}
knitr::include_graphics("~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/figures_external/ASCII-Table.png")
```

# Load the TeDDi data
```{r}
# load data from TeDDi dumps (takes a couple of minutes)
line.data <- read.csv(
  "~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/data/TeDDi/line_sample.csv")
file.data <- read.csv("~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/data/TeDDi/file.csv")
# merge the files
teddi.data <- merge(line.data, file.data, by.x = "file_id", by.y = "id")
```

# Further Sampling
Sample a given number of lines randomly as a comparative sample.
```{r}
set.seed(15022018)
teddi.sample <-sample_n(teddi.data, 1000)
```

# Preprocessing

# Data Cleaning
Remove punctuation for all text lines, as well as ASCII Characters from non-Latin writing systems (this is the most common type of noise in this data).
```{r}
# remove punctuation from all text lines
teddi.sample$text <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", '', teddi.sample$text)
# remove ASCII characters from non-Latin scripts
# the regex "[!-~]" matches ASCII characters (except white spaces)
teddi.sample[teddi.sample$writing_system != "Latn", ]$text <- 
  gsub("[!-~]", '', teddi.sample[teddi.sample$writing_system != "Latn", ]$text)
```

# Transliterate Chinese Characters to Strokes

## Read file with strokes per character
Transliterate Chinese characters to strings of strokes represented by Latin characters.
```{r}
# load stroke transliteration list
stroke.file = "~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/data/TeDDi/zh2letter.txt"
stroke.df <- read.table("~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/data/TeDDi/zh2letter.txt", sep = " ")
# add column names
colnames(stroke.df) <- c("chars","strokes")
# give beginning of signlist
head(stroke.df)
```

## Replace Chinese characters by strokes
```{r}
# select only Hanzi simplified script (ISO code Hans)
hans.data <- teddi.sample[teddi.sample$writing_system == "Hans", ]  
# split into individual characters (list by text line)
hans.list <- strsplit(hans.data$text, split = "")
head(hans.list)
# replace characters with stroke transliterations for each string in list
for (i in 1:length(hans.list)){
  # remove remaining white spaces
  hans.list[[i]] <- hans.list[[i]][hans.list[[i]] != " "]
  hans.list[[i]] <- paste(with(stroke.df, strokes[match(hans.list[[i]], chars)]), collapse = " ")
}
head(hans.list)
# unlist and replace original text column in cmn dataframe
hans.data$text <- unlist(hans.list)
# add comment on stroke transliteration in column "comments"
hans.data$comments <- rep("chars transliterated to strokes", nrow(hans.data))
# add cmn data with strokes to overall data frame
teddi.sample.modified <- rbind(teddi.sample, hans.data) 
```

# Final Preprocessing
Trim white spaces at beginning and end of texts sequences, remove empty text rows (only consisting of white spaces), as well as very short text lines as these can cause NAs in the later calculations. This is the same for other sequences, i.e. paleolithic and proto-cuneiform.
```{r}
teddi.clean <- teddi.sample.modified[teddi.sample.modified$text != "", ]
teddi.clean$text <- trimws(teddi.clean$text)
teddi.clean <- teddi.clean[nchar(teddi.clean$text) > 1, ]
```

# Simple Stats
Some simple stats of the textual data here sampled from TeDDi.
```{r}
# lines of text
nrow(teddi.clean)
# unique ISO codes (i.e. languages)
unique(teddi.clean$iso639_3)
# writing systems
unique(teddi.clean$writing_system)
```

Write to file.
```{r}
# order the columns for convenience
teddi.clean <- teddi.clean[order(teddi.clean$language_name_glotto), ]
# write to file
write.csv(teddi.clean, 
          file = "~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/data/TeDDi/final_sample.csv", row.names = F)
```
